components.local_changes: Separate instance-owned two-PIC x86 boundary model, ICW3 selection, two-phase acknowledgement, fully nested priorities, edge/level requests, separate EOI/AEOI, rotation, special masks and spurious master/slave vectors. Extended against Intel 231468-003; no XT behavior change. Poll, SFNM, buffered and MCS-80/85 explicitly unsupported. No physical timing claim.

Instance-owned architectural-boundary CPU/DMA/ISA ownership, HOLD/HLDA/LOCK arbitration, read-only debug routing and forwarding of board-converted requester-clock waits. One external requester only; no physical ISA cycle timing or PIC/DMA implementation.

Authored synthetic endpoint and architecture-neutral bus/memory checks, an existing-engine clock-math oracle and initial component acceptance sources for 286, Headland, AT arbitration, PIC and DMA, plus extended AT ownership, cleanup, error and debug-isolation tests. Unimplemented components are explicitly skipped, never replaced with success stubs. Added reset-ROM/RAM/AT/PIC/286 board-wiring diagnostic with guest IVT/PIC initialization, IRQ1/9 handlers, HOLD/HLDA, observational DEBUG, native-wait forwarding, interrupted INTA recovery, isolation and partial-construction cleanup; all windows and wait values are synthetic and not PCS286 chipset evidence. No firmware, third-party test vectors or chip implementation copied. Added a new closed-form Group 2 oracle, exhaustive byte/count/carry/status-background cases, sampled word boundaries, every documented opcode/register form, segment overrides, odd split writes and endpoint failure checks. Undefined-flag and zero-count-access choices are tested as emulator policies, not hardware certification. Added an authored sign/magnitude multiplication oracle, exhaustive byte pairs, word sweeps against edge multipliers, immediate/sign-extension and conversion sweeps, aliases, all segment overrides and every fetch/read failure. Undefined flags are checked as preservation policy, without silicon certification. Added an independent unsigned long-division oracle with sign/magnitude conversion for DIV/IDIV, prefix-inclusive #DE frame checks, guest repair/IRET/retry, TF/shadow policies, register aliases, aligned/odd memory/IVT/stack and every-transfer fault injection without rollback. Synthetic tests only, not chip timing or hardware vectors.

Draft C11 CPU interfaces for explicit 286 architectural state, protected-mode hidden caches, board-owned bus accesses, INTA, HOLD/LOCK/shutdown and the existing native-cycle clocked scheduler. Declarations only; no CPU implementation or timing tables copied or provided.

Per-instance 80286 lifecycle, defined reset state, architectural import, 24-bit reset fetch, NOP and boundary HOLD acknowledgement. Private real-mode decoding, MOV, ES/DS reload, register XCHG, binary ALU, TEST, INC/DEC and NEG/NOT with explicit partial-transfer failures. Basic PUSH/POP, near CALL/JMP/RET, Jcc and LOOP/JCXZ added with delayed register/IP commit and no write rollback. PUSHA/POPA and ENTER/LEAVE stage all register changes, preserve original SP/discard its saved slot, mask nesting to five bits and interleave frame reads/writes; unsupported fault/shutdown paths reject explicitly without claiming silicon ordering. Real-mode far JMP EA and memory FF /5 atomically reload CS/IP after successful reads, drop the reset cache base, preserve board-owned A20 and wrap between pointer words as observed in pinned Harris vectors; authored reset, alignment, limits and failure tests added. Logical AF-clear is a deterministic emulator policy, not a silicon claim. Consulted pinned inherited algorithms without globals. MOV/POP SS now reload real-mode caches with separate SS versus INTR-only boundary shadows, preserving deferred events and not consuming inhibition on HOLD/error. All eight direct IN/OUT forms use logical 16-bit I/O transactions, split odd words and commit registers only after success; physical I/O timing remains unknown. Real-mode INTR with two INTA callbacks, NMI and sampled trap entry now stage FLAGS/CS/IP frames and use IDTR; CLI/STI/HLT/IRET cover inhibition, halt wakeup and NMI unblock with inherited 286 real-mode FLAGS masking. Authored endpoint-failure, alignment, priority and cascaded-PIC roundtrip tests do not certify electrical timing. Real-mode INT imm8/INT3/INTO now save post-instruction IP, clear IF/TF on entry and bypass INTA; the documented B-2/later INT single-step rule is used, without early-stepping claims. PUSHF/POPF and LAHF/SAHF, CLC/STC/CMC and CLD/STD preserve 286 FLAGS rules; POPF creates no STI shadow. All vectors, all POPF flag images, alignment, wrap and every endpoint failure are covered by authored tests, not silicon or timing certification. Real-mode far CALL 9A/FF /3 and RETF CA/CB now stage CS/IP/SP until all accesses succeed, preserve FLAGS and NMI blocking, reload real-mode CS and handle parameter discard. Shared FF pointer-word wrap policy and stack preflight remain functional, not silicon fault-order claims. Authored overlap, reset-cache, A20, wrap, all 65536 RETF cleanup values and every-transfer failure tests added. Real-mode LEA, LDS/LES and XLAT now use the explicit EA/data bus: LEA performs no data-segment access; far loads stage both words before replacing a register and DS/ES; XLAT indexes unsigned AL with 16-bit BX wrap and preserves AH. Authored EA/override/register matrices, cache reload, aliases, bounds and every-read failure tests added. LDS/LES pointer wrap follows the inherited word-offset policy without new silicon certification. Memory XCHG, guest faults, protected mode, remaining ISA and physical timing remain pending; strict clocked execution stops without fetching. Real-mode Group 2 ROL/ROR/RCL/RCR/SHL/SHR/SAR now use five-bit counts, staged flag commit and bounded unsigned bit steps. Pinned inherited shift handlers were consulted. Undefined AF is cleared for nonzero shifts and undefined multi-count OF is preserved as explicit emulator policies; zero-count memory reads follow the inherited functional access policy, without physical bus claims. All byte inputs/counts/carry states and word boundary values are checked against an authored closed-form oracle; /6 remains unsupported. Real-mode MUL/IMUL F6/F7 /4,/5, immediate IMUL 69/6B and CBW/CWD now preserve alias-safe source capture and staged architectural commit. Signed conversion uses mathematical subtraction and bounded int32 products, not host signed narrowing or shifts. Undefined multiply S/Z/A/P flags are preserved as explicit emulator policy. Consulted pinned x86_ops_misc.h and x86_ops_mul.h; no timing constants copied. DIV/IDIV remain unsupported pending correct guest divide-error delivery. Real-mode DIV/IDIV now stage quotient/remainder, use widened signed division to avoid host overflow, and deliver synchronous #DE via the existing frame helper with prefix-inclusive fault IP, no error code and no INTA. Boundary reports EXCEPTION vector 0; successful division preserves undefined arithmetic flags as policy. No new sampled trap on fault; clearing a prior SS-deferred trap on fault is explicit pending-hardware policy. Failed frame/IVT endpoints latch stopped without replaying writes; guest #SS/#GP/#DF/shutdown and protected division remain unsupported. Pinned inherited x86_ops_misc.h consulted; no timings or CPU-specific undefined flag hacks copied. Real-mode decimal adjustments DAA/DAS/AAA/AAS/AAM/AAD now stage AX/defined flags; undefined flags are preserved as explicit policy. AAA/AAS use full-AX 286 correction; DAS retains low-stage borrow. AAM/AAD consume immediate radix, including AAD zero; AAM zero delivers shared #DE rather than the inherited base-ten fallback. Pinned x86_ops_bcd.h consulted and recorded, authors retained; no timing copied. Authored scalar, valid packed-decimal arithmetic, prefix, transfer failure and guest self-repair/IRET tests added. Nondecimal/invalid-BCD edge coverage is functional, not new chip capture certification. Unprefixed real-mode MOVS/STOS/LODS/CMPS/SCAS byte/word now execute a single element independently of CX; source overrides and fixed ES destination, DF/16-bit index wrap, staged AX/index/FLAGS commit and shared subtraction flags. Pinned x86_ops_string.h consulted; inherited CMPS destination-first read order retained as functional policy, not hardware fault-precedence evidence. Host failures latch stopped without replay or rolling back completed writes; inherited post-guest-abort index quirks are not used to simulate missing guest faults. Authored independent comparison oracle, segment/DF/alignment/CX matrices, overlap, wrap, partial-write failure, TF and HOLD tests. REP, string I/O, guest segment-fault delivery, protection and physical timing remain pending.
Draft independent memory routing and register interface, with explicit requester/A20 and memory-clock waits. No register implementation or inherited fixed remapping logic.

New per-instance declaration boundary for future IOC02 register work. Existing code was consulted to identify integration responsibilities; no register semantics, firmware workaround or implementation was ported.

Draft contracts for board arbitration/ISA resources, cascaded PIC, dual-width DMA, timer readback, AT RTC, separate keyboard/controller protocols, WD37C65B, ATA PIO and synchronized clock links. No device implementations or firmware-derived routines copied.
Draft standalone palette/DAC interface and explicit single-owner boundary with existing PVGA1A. No new video or DAC emulation.

New typed machine configuration, board-glue declarations and standalone C/C++ header compilation checks. Contract-only system is not registered or linked into frontends. Canonical evidence and inherited composition were consulted without porting behavioural code; future ports require their own exact provenance.

Instance-owned RAM and copied/interleaved firmware storage, failure-safe construction and bounded resolved-offset transactions. No physical decode, A20, remap, chipset state or timing claims. Authored independently of inherited behavioural implementation; existing machine configuration contract supplies input layout.

Initial deterministic engine, rational CPU and dynamically controlled timed-device clock domains with an exact queryable source-cycle cursor, scheduler, host-neutral physical input and guest-owned keyboard-indicator value types, XRGB8888 framebuffer value types and caller-owned block-media contract; exact integral-period clock advances use an overflow-checked constant-time path while fractional domains retain the portable general algorithm, and the scheduler reuses an exact nearest deadline until a successful event/source mutation invalidates it

Host-independent address-space bus with validated debug and initiator-held lock transaction attributes plus an optional address-space-filtered observer for deterministic external traces without callbacks on unrelated memory, I/O, program or data traffic
Host-allocated RAM and ROM regions with endian-neutral bus transactions
Independent floppy-drive geometry, atomic media replacement/ejection, change state and raw-sector access over the host-neutral block-media contract

Replaced global CPU state and legacy memory coupling with explicit per-instance model profiles and bus transactions; added a positively classified Intel 8088 profile sourced from Intel documentation plus separately identified original-silicon evidence, with an 8-bit external bus, ordered byte-split word memory and I/O transfers, a four-byte byte-fetch queue, Intel FLAGS/reset/interrupt behavior, no NEC 8080 mode, a complete primary/grouped opcode decision map, physical aliases kept distinct from the published ISA, Intel timing remaining explicitly unknown, and no new 8088 implementation copied from PCem, 86Box or MartyPC; retained one 16-bit little-endian transfer for aligned V30 word memory accesses and two byte transfers for odd words; added a versioned architectural-state transfer and single-boundary step contract for conformance, including distinct maskable and segment-transfer shadows plus latched NMI and single-step requests; added a hardware-vector-validated primary ALU matrix, NEC 82h immediate alias, DAA/DAS/AAA/AAS and AAM/AAD adjustment semantics, CWD and INT3/INTO; completed both TEST aliases and tested arithmetic and logical operations including immediate groups, byte/word signed and unsigned multiply, signed and unsigned byte/word divide with interrupt-zero faults and the observed NEC byte-IDIV -128 boundary, NEG, CBW, accumulator TEST and XLAT; extended the 80186-compatible V30 set with PUSHA/POPA, sign-extending and word immediate PUSH, both immediate IMUL forms, signed CHKIND/BOUND with BRK 5, full-byte-count C0h/C1h shifts, PREPARE and DISPOSE, and INSB/INSW/OUTSB/OUTSW with REP and explicit memory/I/O bus transactions, while explicitly rejecting NEC-undefined opcodes 63h and F1h plus immediate-shift group /6; added conditional flow, ModR/M memory operands, explicit ES/CS/SS/DS overrides, stack operations, direct and indirect near/far calls and jumps, near/far return forms with caller cleanup, SAHF/LAHF, canonical V30 PSW images and snapshot state for the MD write gate, plus the documented 8080 emulation opcode map with physical register/flag mapping, BRKEM/CALLN/RETEM and native interrupt round trips while rejecting undefined aliases and nesting; added NEC V30 TEST1/CLR1/SET1/NOT1 bit operations with validated Group 3 encodings, packed-BCD ADD4S/SUB4S/CMP4S strings, ROL4/ROR4 nibble rotations and register/immediate INS/EXT bit fields over portable memory, and a host-neutral FPO1/FPO2/POLL coprocessor contract that exposes documented dummy memory reads, explicit absent-device behavior and propagated callback errors without embedding floating-point execution; added software and callback-based real-mode interrupts with documented NMI-over-INT-over-single-step priority, EI/segment-transfer acceptance delays, HALT wake-up and interruptible REP restart at retained prefixes, complete D0-D3 rotate/shift groups, general byte/word XCHG, flag-control operations, byte and word string operations including CMPS and SCAS with REP/REPE/REPNE plus V30 REPC/REPNC carry conditions, BUSLOCK propagation through explicit bus transaction attributes and locked-block interrupt deferral, acceptance of observed non-string REP prefixes, ROM-checksum and memory-check paths, prefix-aware instruction tracing and full basic-register inspection; added executable classification of all native and emulation primary opcodes, NEC Group 3 extensions and grouped ModR/M operation fields, with reserved and model-inapplicable forms remaining explicit unsupported results; added a versioned host-neutral timing observer which separates exact documented native execution clocks, including decoded effective-address parity, entry-stack parity, counted shifts, PREPARE, NEC Group 3 and completed memory/I/O string formulas, and documented arithmetic, bit-field and CHKIND timing ranges from logical bus transactions, reported device waits and prefetch-queue invalidation events, while leaving exact realised data-dependent clocks, interrupted string fragments and POLL timing explicitly unclassified; added a real per-instance six-byte V30 instruction queue and PFP with aligned word or odd byte demand fetch, persistent prefetched bytes, explicit control-transfer invalidation, queue observation and synthetic self-modifying-code coverage; timing-observation version 8 composes demand-prefetch, queue-read and documented execution clocks into a complete boundary duration only for uncontended native instructions, preserves execution ranges, reclassifies cross-boundary speculative fetch phases when they become demand stalls, advances the shared T1/T2/T3/Tw/T4 BCU during every queue-read predecode clock, keeps instruction fetch outside BUSLOCK attributes, and routes every memory and I/O operand through the BCU while reporting prefetch handoff and operand occupancy separately until their EXU positions are known; version 9 introduces explicit EXU-clock placement, ports the inherited internal-wait and operand order for all eight native IN/OUT forms, distinguishes operand wait extensions, and publishes a complete boundary only when the full execution timeline is proven; version 10 places each native prefix's documented execution interval at decode time, allowing prefixed direct I/O to retain a complete timeline while other operand-bearing forms remain explicitly unresolved; version 11 places the four direct accumulator-memory MOV forms and XLAT, including their inherited internal clocks and both physical transfers of odd words; version 12 places MOV r/m,reg memory loads after three inherited internal clocks and memory stores after five while leaving register forms on the bus-free path; version 13 places read-only ModR/M ALU memory forms at their inherited offsets, including CMP in both encoding directions, while leaving read-modify-write destinations unresolved; version 14 places both bus transfers of ModR/M ALU read-modify-write destinations and preserves the inherited four-clock computation interval between them; version 15 places ModR/M TEST reads and both XCHG memory transfers at their inherited offsets, including prefixed forms; version 16 restores the inherited operand-before-immediate ordering for ALU groups 80h-83h and places their memory read, computation interval and optional write; version 17 places segment-register MOV memory transfers and immediate-to-r/m MOV groups C6h-C7h while preserving bus-free register forms; version 18 places Group 3 F6h-F7h memory reads plus TEST immediate and NOT/NEG write intervals without collapsing documented multiply or signed-divide timing ranges; version 19 places FEh/FFh byte and word memory INC/DEC reads, computation intervals and writes while leaving the remaining FFh control forms unresolved; version 20 places single-word register, segment, flags and immediate stack pushes and pops, including odd-stack transfer splits; version 21 places normal, repeated and zero-count STOS/SCAS transfers while keeping interrupted repeat fragments unclassified; version 22 adds explicit BCU prefetch suspension and places relative near CALL and near RET stack transfers around their target-queue flush; version 23 places normal, repeated, segment-overridden and zero-count MOVS/LODS transfers including odd words; version 24 classifies the documented four-clock accumulator-immediate TEST forms; version 25 places both LES/LDS far-pointer word reads including odd pointers and segment overrides; version 26 places software INT vector reads and interrupt-frame writes in inherited order and places IRET stack reads around prefetch suspension and target-queue flush; version 27 places register and memory indirect near CALL target reads and stack writes around prefetch suspension and target-queue flush; added a strict clocked-engine step adapter that publishes only complete exact scalar boundary durations and rejects unresolved ranges without silently selecting an endpoint; version 28 resolves unsigned MULU's documented one-clock range with the inherited V30 microcode's high-half condition while retaining signed arithmetic ranges; version 29 places accepted NMI and maskable interrupt boundaries with documented V30 acceptance costs, three alignment-sensitive stack writes and explicit BCU prefetch handoff; version 30 classifies the documented seven-clock immediately-ready POLL case while retaining a strict unknown result for repeated busy waits; version 31 places the two alignment-sensitive stack reads and target-queue flush of far returns, with and without immediate caller cleanup, in inherited microcode order; version 32 places Group 5 PUSH source reads, the inherited internal interval and alignment-sensitive stack writes, and corrects both PUSH SP encodings to store the decremented stack pointer; version 33 places register and memory indirect near-jump target reads before inherited prefetch suspension and target-queue invalidation; version 34 places normal, repeated and zero-count CMPS source and destination reads while retaining interrupted repeat fragments as unknown; version 35 places both pointer reads, both alignment-sensitive stack writes and target-queue invalidation for indirect far calls; version 36 places POP r/m16 stack reads and destination writes while preserving pre-pop effective-address calculation and independent source/destination alignment; version 37 places both pointer reads of indirect far jumps before inherited prefetch suspension and target-queue invalidation, including odd pointers and segment overrides; version 38 places both stack writes and target-queue invalidation for direct far calls in inherited microcode order

Replaced global devices and direct CPU coupling with opaque single-instance components: an 8237 programming and request-state core with synchronous device-facing memory transfers, external XT page latches with full-byte readback, separately masked physical address outputs, explicit channel mapping and effective addresses, and a single edge-triggered 8259A whose request inputs must remain asserted until acknowledgement; scheduler-facing adapters build as a separate optional target

Reworked the inherited uPD765-compatible command path into an opaque AT-register component with explicit drives, IRQ6 callback, DMA channel 2 transfers and raw-sector media; removed global drive tables, host files, UI state and real-time timers; declared and enforced a 4096-byte maximum sector payload before DMA or media access; reject terminal count before a complete sector instead of reporting a partial DMA read as success, while allowing terminal count after a complete sector to finish a command before an extended EOT

Reduced the inherited parallel subsystem to an opaque caller-owned SPP register component with explicit output and ACK-interrupt callbacks; removed global port tables, host character devices, EPP/ECP, DMA, timers and threads

Reduced the inherited UART model to an opaque NS16450 register core with divisor latch, interrupt priority, modem/data loopback and explicit host callbacks; removed 16550 FIFOs, global COM tables, mouse coupling, host serial backends and real-time baud scheduling

Ported the measured 8253 edge-state core behind an opaque bus component, removing legacy globals, host timers and platform callbacks while retaining modes 0-5, BCD, gates, latches and output transitions; added exact next-output transition queries and binary-counter batch advancement with an exact BCD fallback

Optional composition adapter that advances the independent 8253 model lazily between exact output-transition deadlines, synchronizes state before I/O and keeps scheduler ownership outside the chip core

Ported the PCS 86 B0h-B7h control window and E0h-EFh counter/alarm RAM to an opaque, deterministic component with BCD calendar progression, IRQ generation, checksum repair, caller-owned persistence and optional synchronization hooks that keep scheduler ownership outside the chip model

Optional composition adapter that advances the MM58167 on an exact one-megahertz microsecond domain, synchronizes before I/O and persistent-state operations, and schedules only millisecond and rollover-window transitions

Isolated the PVGA1A register files, Paradise extension lock, DAC state and 256 KiB planar VRAM behind generic memory and I/O buses; added ordered multi-byte I/O transactions so a V30 word access can program adjacent indexed-register ports without a CPU or firmware special case; added deterministic text-mode geometry and XRGB8888 rasterization from the programmed character, attribute, font and palette state. Text cursor shape, disable state, skew, character address and VSYNC-derived blink phase are rendered from CRTC state and explicit emulated time. Standard four-plane 16-colour and chain-4 256-colour output derive geometry, display start, offset, maximum-scan-line repetition, double-scan, Paradise PR4 pixel rate and palette selection from register state without BIOS mode-number cases. CGA-compatible packed shift modes, line compare/panning and scan-event generation remain absent, and input-status timing is an explicit deterministic bring-up approximation

Instance-owned register file, mirrored 16 KiB VRAM, M15 monochrome-port alias, 40/80-column text and 320/640-pixel CGA-compatible raster output to palette indices. Firmware glyph data is caller-provided and LCD green mapping belongs to the machine. Status timing is a declared virtual-time approximation; undocumented 16-colour modes, external composite output and exact panel timing are not modeled.

Opaque session lifecycle, typed machine factory with an explicit validated choice between instruction-tick and nanosecond clocked engine contracts, machine reset and inspection hooks, optional host-neutral framebuffer discovery/rendering operations with an explicit deterministic emulated-time input, normalized physical-key input events and guest-owned keyboard-indicator queries independent of host lock state and guest scan-code sets, generic caller-owned storage-media replacement, and opaque named-state export while a machine is live
Deterministic host adapter for tests and headless use

Frontend-neutral machine adapter registry, declarative asset, replaceable-storage and persistent-state requirements, typed configuration preparation over caller-owned blobs and block media, and deterministic, restored or depleted PCS 86 RTC initial state supplied outside the engine; optional file helpers remain separate from the adapter contract. An opt-in read-only debug observer reports ordered instruction, I/O and accepted-interrupt events without exposing paths, host APIs or frontend types to the machine

Qt6 application shell whose available products are mapped declaratively from the historical catalogue to frontend adapters, with a dedicated definition-rate-paced session worker, queued lifecycle, normalized keyboard and read-only removable-media commands, guest-controlled Caps/Num/Scroll presentation, generation-safe XRGB8888 frame publication, explicit session lifecycle controls, host-side presentation scaling, selectable Qt OpenGL and software surfaces, a non-destructive scanline/vignette CRT profile, clean source-frame capture, persistent user display preferences and frontend-owned battery-backed named state with an explicit depleted-battery policy; Windows host-only high-resolution worker waits with command wakeup and a portable fallback, plus opt-in input/render/paint-submission diagnostics without key contents

Registry-driven command-line frontend independent of Qt, with host-side firmware loading, read-only file-backed block media, explicit generic persistent-state load/save or depleted-state selection, deterministic execution and engine-mode reporting including available RTC calendar state, and framebuffer capture; consumes the shared frontend adapter contract without direct machine-system dependencies. Optional bounded failure diagnostics retain a configurable interleaved event tail plus a fixed interrupt-boundary history and full CPU register state

Replaced legacy timers, globals, host image tables and direct PIC/DMA calls with caller-owned block media, explicit bus/DMA/IRQ contracts, deterministic PIO and DMA phases, configurable geometry, controller gating, structured state inspection and an explicit pending-service contract; unsupported commands report the hardware illegal-command completion rather than being silently accepted

Machine-selected timed-source adapter for deferred XTA DMA service; remains disarmed while idle, retries a pending transfer at the declared functional interval and makes no claim about mechanical disk timing

Isolated the M15 MSM6242 register calendar behind a typed, instance-owned I/O device. Caller-owned initial state and explicit virtual-second advancement replace global host-time and NVR state. Models 12/24-hour BCD calendar, HOLD, STOP, REST and 30-second adjustment; BUSY timing, IRQ pulse output and TEST mode remain unsupported. The source retains the inherited BSD terms in full.

Internal M15 bring-up system with instance-owned board-switch and keyboard state, typed firmware, floppy and RTC configuration, rational-clock Intel 8088, memory, PIC, PIT, DMA, FDC, V6355D presentation and deterministic MSM6242 calendar. The M15-specific switch, 05h-to-82h identification and XT-compatible Port B strobe behavior derive from the inherited pilot; normalized-key to guest-byte mapping is adapted from the portable PCS86. A bounded per-instance scan queue, virtual-millisecond delivery, IRQ1 and explicit Port B acknowledgement replace inherited globals and polling fallback. This is a compatibility stream, not a validated physical M15 keyboard protocol. Generic components are independently linked. No BIOS, ROM or media are included.

Isolated the documented V30, RAM, ROM, DMA, PIC, independently clocked PIT and MM58167, PVGA1A core and motherboard register map behind a typed machine factory; added explicit reset, inspection, interrupt routing, exact rational device clocks, caller-owned MM58167 initial state and opaque RTC state export, NMI/open-bus behavior, diagnostic and memory-control latches, configurable 0/384/1920 KiB onboard EMS with software-derived relocatable frames at 40000h-9FFFFh, independent selector banks gated by port 6Bh and conventional-memory fallback, immutable system-EPROM reads with hardware-like ignored CPU writes, unpopulated-option-ROM open bus, video-arbitration latches, runtime framebuffer publication, gated SPP and NS16450 devices, dual board keyboard/mouse protocol queues, normalized Set 1 keyboard delivery and keyboard EDh indicator state, baseline three-button PS/2 stream/remote packets and command state over neutral relative-pointer events, a uPD765-compatible controller with IRQ6/DMA2 and validated media replacement, and the onboard XTA gate with IRQ5/DMA3 and the active-low presence jumper. Accepted PIC vectors can be observed through an optional read-only callback used by frontend diagnostics. The V30, PIT and RTC share deterministic nanosecond virtual time; XTA DMA service uses a demand-driven timed source at the declared 32-microsecond functional interval instead of an always-running machine callback. Explicitly model the absent AT CMOS data port 71h as open bus, matching inherited device composition without adding a CMOS or changing the MM58167; model the inherited unclaimed 88h-9Fh region as open bus, and explicitly supply absent-coprocessor POLL ready without implementing an 8087; configuration version 6 can forward the versioned V30 timing observer to diagnostics, and the firmware probe reports exact, ranged and unknown boundary coverage per effective opcode plus the first unknown boundary context; the machine registers the V30 at 10 MHz, PIT at the exact divided PC crystal, RTC at one megahertz and XTA service at its explicit functional rate in the clocked runtime
